info.title: Mercury core API
info.description: The core's HTTP API: the bodies of every request and response, and the events of a question's stream.

200.description: The questions of the window by outcome, channel, project, class, refusal and judge, their durations and cost, the sign-offs, today's spend against the budget, the alerts that hold and the settings the core runs with. Counts and metadata only: no question's text, answer or fact. The read is itself an audit row, `admin_viewed`.

400.description: A window other than 24h, 7d or 30d, or another parameter.

200.description: Everyone, disabled people too: role, grants with approver flags and what each lets them ask, tokens by public id, label and dates (never a secret), their questions of the last 30 days. Read-only: people, roles, grants and tokens change through the admin commands on the server. The read is itself an audit row, `admin_viewed`.

400.description: A parameter; the route takes none.

200.description: Every project projects.yaml lists or a probe registered: its probe's state, freshness, access mode and what limited it, its quarantine, and the people granted it. Read-only: a quarantine changes through the admin commands on the server, an access mode through the files there. The read is itself an audit row, `admin_viewed`.

400.description: A parameter; the route takes none.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `pending`, the only one; it may be left out.

200.description: The held answers, pending and unexpired, of every project the caller approves, oldest first; the caller's own questions come with asked_by_me and without draft and flags, since the asker reads nothing of a held answer before the decision. Empty for someone who approves nothing.

400.description: A status other than pending, or another parameter.

204.description: Decided: the question goes on with the draft unchanged (answer, done) or with refused rejected_by_approver, the note as its hint.

400.description: A malformed body, or a rejection without a note of 1 to 500 characters on one line.

403.description: The caller's own question; or with the session cookie but not from the web client's own page.

404.description: No such approval, or one of a project the caller doesn't approve.

409.description: Already decided, or expired after 24 hours.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The row's project, else its question's.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The asker's e-mail address, or for a row without a question the one its payload names; case ignored.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: A token's public id: its questions, and the rows without a question that name it (sign-ins, refusals, its creation and revocation).

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The question's class; rows without a question don't match.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: The question's status: running, pending_signoff, delivered, refused, clarify or failed; rows without a question don't match.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: From this time on, included: RFC 3339, or YYYY-MM-DD for its midnight UTC.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Before this time, not included: RFC 3339, or YYYY-MM-DD for its midnight UTC.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 500; 100 by default.

200.description: A page of rows in seq order: every row, for an admin, the only one who reads the audit.

400.description: A filter, the limit or the cursor doesn't parse.

403.description: Not an admin. What Mercury did with a person's own question is in its events.

200.description: Every matching row up to the last one at the request's start, one AuditItem per line in seq order, streamed. The export is itself an audit row, `audit_exported`, written first.

400.description: `format` isn't jsonl, or a filter doesn't parse.

200.description: The projects the person may ask about.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters; a repeat returns the first question's id.

400.description: A malformed body or key; a clarify of a question that isn't the caller's or didn't end with a clarify; a follows that isn't the caller's own question rejected by an approver (the same message whatever the reason).

403.description: With the session cookie but not from the web client's own page (Origin, X-Mercury-Client).

429.description: Over the token's rate limit; see Retry-After.

404.description: Not the caller's question, or no such question.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Replay the events after this one.

200.description: Server-sent events: `event:` an event's name, `id:` its audit seq, `data:` its data (see the Event schema). Ends after a terminal event.

404.description: Not the caller's question, or no such question.

204.description: Recorded; a second one replaces the first.

403.description: With the session cookie but not from the web client's own page (Origin, X-Mercury-Client).

404.description: Not the caller's question, or no such question.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: The web client's own origin, as the server is set up with it (MERCURY_PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

204.description: Signed in: the cookie `__Host-mercury_session` is set (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/), for the server's session time and never beyond the token's expiry.

401.description: No valid token: unauthenticated, or token_expired.

403.description: Not from the web client's own page: the Origin or the X-Mercury-Client header is wrong or missing.

429.description: Too many sign-ins from this address; see Retry-After.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: The web client's own origin, as the server is set up with it (MERCURY_PUBLIC_ORIGIN).

204.description: Signed out: the session is ended and the cookie cleared.

403.description: Not from the web client's own page.

Accepted.description: `202` to `POST /v1/questions`, and the data of the `accepted` event.

follows.description:
In the `accepted` event of a question asked again after a rejection: the rejected question
its `follows` named. Left out otherwise, and always from the `202`.

AccessLimit.description: What lowered the probe's access mode below the one asked for.

AccessMode.description: How much of a repository the probe reads, ordered so the strictest of several is the `min`.

AdminAlert.description: One of the three alerts `mercury-core admin status` says.

oneOf.description: The judge the questions ended on; `null` but for `judge_degraded`.
The silent probe's project; `null` for the other kinds.

since.description:
Since when it holds: the first degraded ending, or the probe's last registration; `null`
for the spend, and for a probe never seen.

oneOf.description: Today's spend and the daily budget; `null` but for `spend`.

AdminGrant.description: A project granted, or the pseudo-project `portfolio`.

classes.description:
What the grant lets its person ask: the classes of their role in `policies.yaml` and the
project's manifest combined, as the core applies them. `null` when the project has no
manifest yet (it can't be asked) or the files can't be read.

AdminOverview.description:
`GET /v1/admin/overview?window=…`: the questions asked in the window and what became of them,
today's spend, the alerts that hold, and the settings the core runs with.

askers.description: How many people asked in the window.

channels.description: `cli`, `web` and `mcp`, each listed even with nothing asked.

classes.description: The classes the questions were given, the most first.

duration_ms.description:
How long the questions that finished in the window took, from asked to ended, leaving out
those held for a sign-off, whose time includes the wait for the approver.

judge.description: Which judge answered the questions that ended in the window, by the weakest any stage had.

projects.description: The projects asked about, the most asked first.

refusals.description: Why questions were refused, the most first.

series.description:
The window in buckets, oldest first, the empty ones included; the first starts at or
before `since`.

signoffs.description: The sign-offs of the window's questions.

totals.description: Every question asked in the window, by outcome.

until.description: The request's time, the window's end.

AdminPeople.description:
`GET /v1/admin/people`: everyone in the database, disabled people too, with their grants,
what each grant lets them ask, and their tokens.

classes_known.description:
False when `policies.yaml` or `projects.yaml` can't be read: every grant's `classes` is
then `null`.

projects.description: The projects `projects.yaml` lists, which a grant may name; empty when it can't be read.

questions_30d.description: The questions they asked in the last 30 days.

oneOf.description: What kept it below `access_max`; `null` when nothing did.

quarantine_reason.description: The reason the admin gave, while it is quarantined.

status.description: At the time of the request: a healthy probe silent for three minutes shows as stale.

AdminRepositories.description:
`GET /v1/admin/repositories`: every project `projects.yaml` lists or a probe registered, with
its probe and the people who may ask about it.

oneOf.description: The most `projects.yaml` lets its probe read; `null` as for `display_name`.

display_name.description:
From `projects.yaml`; `null` for a probe registered under a project the file doesn't list,
or when it can't be read.

people.description: The people granted the project, by e-mail address.

oneOf.description: `null` until the project's probe has registered.

questions_30d.description: The questions asked about it in the last 30 days.

label.description: What the admin named it for, the device say.

Answer.description: An answer that passed the output checks, with the facts it cites. Also the `answer` event.

text.description: Plain text for the person, the citations removed.

asked_by_me.description: The caller's own question, which they can't approve; it comes without `draft` and `flags`.

draft.description:
Exactly what approving delivers. Left out of the caller's own question: the asker reads
nothing of a held answer before the decision.

flags.description: The draft's flagged sentences. Left out of the caller's own question, as the draft is.

oneOf.description: `null` for a portfolio answer.

ApprovalDecision.description: `POST /v1/approvals/{id}`. A rejection needs a note, which the asker sees as the hint.

ApprovalList.description: `GET /v1/approvals?status=…`: the held answers of the approver's projects.

AskCodeArgs.description:
The arguments of `ask_code`: the asker's question after the project's redaction rules, and
nothing else.

AuditItem.description:
One audit row. `GET /v1/audit/export` writes the same rows, one JSON object per line. With
`payload_sha256` and `prev_hash` a row's `hash` can be recomputed without the database:
`SHA-256(prev_hash ‖ seq ‖ len(type) ‖ type ‖ payload_sha256 ‖ at)`, `seq` as 8 big-endian
bytes, `len(type)` as one byte, `at` written with milliseconds.

payload.description: The event's data; `null` once retention deleted it. The hash still covers its digest.

payload_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the payload's stored JSON, kept when retention deletes the payload.

prev_hash.description: The previous row's `hash`; 64 zeros before the first row.

AuditPage.description: `GET /v1/audit`: a page of audit rows, one per event, in `seq` order.

next.description: The cursor of the next page, `null` on the last one.

Bucket.description: How the overview's series cuts its window.

Channel.description: Where a question came from: its `questions.channel`.

CheckLine.description:
A check of the judge's catalogue and the thresholds it is held to; a threshold the check
doesn't use is `null`.

oneOf.description: The judge's probability; left out when a rule decided.

CheckSource.description: What decided a check: a rule, or the judge that answered.

Clarify.description: The question can't go on without the person's choice; it ends here.

cost_usd.description: What the question cost until it asked back.

oneOf.description: The weakest judge any stage had; `null` when no judge answered before it.

of.description: The question that ended with the `clarify`.

id.description: The project id or the class; sent back as `clarify.option`.

Classified.description: The question's class and the input checks.

ComposerMode.description: Who wrote an answer: the composer model, or the template composer when the model couldn't.

Deny.description: What a project refuses: a whole question class, or a topic the checks look for.

judge_mode.description: The weakest judge any stage had.

Durations.description: Each `null` when nothing finished in the window.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every error: for requests that can't start. A question that starts and is then
refused ends with a `refused` event instead.

EventError.description: The question failed after it started.

cost_usd.description: What the question cost until it failed.

oneOf.description: The weakest judge any stage had; `null` when no judge answered before the failure.

Evidence.description:
What a fact rests on. Deserializing rejects a state that doesn't fit the type, and a `ref` on
CI runs or releases.

oneOf.description: `#<number>` for pull requests and issues when the policy shows references, else `null`.

EvidenceState.description: The states of every evidence type in one list; [`Evidence`] checks that the pair fits.

Fact.description: One structured statement about a piece of work.

people.description: Only when the effective policy shows people; otherwise empty.

title_withheld.description: `true` when the title failed a rule or a check and was replaced.

Flag.description: A sentence of the draft that a check flagged, with the check and its probability.

Grant.description: A project the person was granted, or the pseudo-project `portfolio`.

signoff.description: Its answers wait for an approver.

blocked.description: It carries one of the manifest's blocking labels.

ItemSignals.description: The states the status rules read.

issues.description: The linked issues, or the issue itself; at most 20.

oneOf.description: `null` for an issue on its own.

JudgeContext.description: Repository texts the judge may see as context.

none.description: No judge answered: a question refused before any check ran.

JudgeMode.description: Which judge decided, from the strongest to the most degraded.

JudgeReply.description:
The core's reply: the request's purpose, the judge that answered, and one answer per item in
the request's order. Numbers and enums only.

JudgeRequest.description: `POST /internal/judge`: one purpose, 1 to 200 items, each id once.

JudgeText.description: A repository text for the judge; the core redacts it before the judge reads it.

Judged.description: The output checks: how many sentences, how many were stripped, how many held for sign-off.

oneOf.description:
The lowest probability that the answer is fine, over the checks a judge answered on the
sentences the person reads, delivered or held: a check's `p` when its polarity in
`checks.yaml` is `legit`, `1 - p` when it is `risk`. Left out, like a check's `p`, when only
rules decided or there was nothing to check.

KindItem.description: An item whose kind the labels didn't settle: a title, at least one label, or both.

labels.description: Empty when the manifest's `judge_context` leaves labels out; at most 20.

oneOf.description: `null` when the manifest's `judge_context` leaves titles out.

MeToken.description: The token the request came with.

oneOf.description: `jev` or `chat` for the judge's roles; `null` for the planner and the composer.

ModuleName.description: A module name from the probe's describe tool, or Other.

oneOf.description: The option picked after a `clarify`; the text stays the same.

The caller's own question that an approver rejected (`rejected_by_approver`), asked again
here in new words or the same; the audit links the two.

OutcomeCounts.description: Questions by what became of them; each question is in exactly one.

degraded.description: Delivered, judged by the chat fallback or the rules.

held.description: Went to a sign-off, whatever was decided.

other.description: A clarify, a failure, or still running.

OverviewWindow.description: The span `GET /v1/admin/overview` counts over, back from the request's time.

PendingSignoff.description: The answer waits for an approver.

Plan.description: The tool calls the fixed class table chose, with the arguments the planner filled.

access.description: Can only lower what the token and the admin's cap allow.

exclude.description: Globs deleted right after a snapshot is unpacked, never indexed.

judge_context.description: Which repository texts the judge may see. No default: the owner states it.

module_labels.description: Labels that put pull requests and issues into a module; the only mapping in `metadata` mode.

propertyNames.description: A module name from the probe's describe tool, or Other.

modules.description: Globs that map files to modules, in the order they are tried.

propertyNames.description: A module name from the probe's describe tool, or Other.

ProbeRegistration.description: `POST /internal/probes/register`, from a probe on start and every 60 s.

access.description: The effective mode: the strictest of the token, the manifest and the admin's cap.

oneOf.description: What lowered the mode, or `null` when nothing did.

manifest_hash.description: The SHA-256 of the manifest the probe read.

as_of.description: When the probe's data was last fresh.

oneOf.description: `null` for the questions that never reached a project (refused or clarified first).

ProjectList.description: `GET /v1/projects`: the projects the person may ask about.

ProjectPicked.description: The project the question is about, and who chose it.

classes.description: The classes the effective policy allows this person here.

oneOf.description: `null` until the project's probe has registered.

QuestionClass.description: What kind of question it is. One judge choice over these classifies every question.

oneOf.description: `null` until a judge has answered.

RedactRule.description: One redaction rule: a regular expression and the literal text that replaces each match.

RedactedQuestion.description: The asker's question after the redaction rules, on one line: a tool argument, never part of a reply.

Refusal.description: Why a question was refused, and what the person can do instead. Also the `refused` event.

Refused.description: The question was refused: why, what the person can do instead, and what it cost until then.

cost_usd.description: What the question cost until it was refused.

oneOf.description: The weakest judge any stage had; `null` when no judge answered before the refusal.

Role.description: Who a token belongs to. Approving is a flag on a user, not a role.

SafeText.description: One line of redacted text: no code, paths, identifiers, URLs, e-mail addresses or secrets.

version.description: The product version, `0.0.0` until a release.

Settings.description: What the core runs with, from its files: shown, never changed here.

oneOf.description: `null` when `models.yaml` can't be read.

checks.description: The judge's checks and their thresholds; `null` when `checks.yaml` can't be read.

models.description: Each model role's backend; `null` when `models.yaml` can't be read.

SignoffReason.description: Why an answer waits for an approver.

oneOf.description: `global_daily_usd` from `models.yaml`; `null` when the file can't be read.

day.description: The UTC day the spend is counted on.

people.description: The people who spent anything today, the most first.

oneOf.description: `per_user_daily_usd` from `models.yaml`; `null` when the file can't be read.
`null` for a person no longer in the database.

StatusAnswer.description: The candidate the judge chose, and its probability.

StatusItem.description: A status the rules couldn't settle: the statuses they point to, and what the judge may read.

labels.description: Empty when the manifest's `judge_context` leaves labels out; at most 20.

oneOf.description: `null` when the manifest's `judge_context` leaves titles out.

Tested.description: `missing` only where the probe counts tests, never in `metadata` mode.

TitleAnswer.description: The probability that the title holds code, an identifier, a path, a secret or a client name.

TitleItem.description: A title the rules let through, for the judge to look at again.

ToolChecked.description: The checks on one call, before it runs.

ToolName.description:
A probe tool. The set is fixed by the probe's access mode; a probe that offers a different one
is quarantined.

ToolResult.description: What one call returned, counted, never shown.

access.description: The probe's effective mode when it answered.

oneOf.description:
The lowest probability that the reply is fine, over the call's data checks a judge
answered (`field_contains_agent_instruction` on each text of the reply, findings
included): a check's `p` when its polarity in `checks.yaml` is `legit`, `1 - p` when it is
`risk`. Left out, like a check's `p`, when only rules decided or there was nothing to check.

withheld_fields.description: Text values a data check withheld, as JSON Pointers into the reply.

Verdict.description: A check's outcome, ordered so the strictest of several is the `max`.

session.name: __Host-mercury_session
session.description: The web client's session. A request that changes state with it must send Origin (the server's own origin) and X-Mercury-Client: web, or it gets 403. Never on /mcp.
